issues.evidence: གཡེལ་པ་མེད་པར is "without negligence/laxity" (Skt atandritena "without sloth"); bo-mipham 5-12 and bo-rangjung 5-12 gloss it as constant, unlapsing reliance (གཡེལ་བ་མེད་པར ... རྒྱུན་དུ་བསྟེན་པ), not lack of vacillation.

issues.span: Just as the perfection of wisdom is empty of characteristics
issues.evidence: ཤེས་རབ་ཕ་རོལ་ཕྱིན་པ་མཚན་ཉིད་སྟོང་ is read in bo-mipham 5-15 and bo-khenrab 5-15 (citing the Eight Thousand) as "the characteristic of the perfection of wisdom is emptiness" (སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་ཀྱི་མཚན་ཉིད་); Skt prajñāpāramitā śūnyatā lakṣaṇena = "has emptiness as its characteristic". bo-rangjung 5-15 allows "empty of characteristic" only as a second option, and the next line ("the characteristics of all phenomena ... similar to that") presupposes that emptiness is the characteristic.
issues.fix: Just as the perfection of wisdom has emptiness as its characteristic,

issues.span: Completely famished sentient beings desire food
issues.evidence: The commentaries do not read ལྟོགས་པ "famished" but ཡོངས་སུ་རྟོག་པ / ཡོངས་སུ་རྟོགས་པ "fully conceptualizing" (bo-mipham 5-16 ཡོངས་སུ་རྟོག་པ་ཅན་དུ་གྱུར་པའི་དབང་གིས ... ཟས་ལ་འདོད་པ་སྐྱེ་བར་བྱེད; bo-rangjung 5-16 and bo-khenrab 5-16 ཡོངས་སུ་རྟོགས་པས), matching Skt parikalpayamāna "imagining"; "food" is explained as the objects of desire (འདོད་ཡོན་གྱི་ཟས). The Tibetan as given may be a scribal variant; the English follows it against the commentarial reading.
issues.fix: Sentient beings, fully conceptualizing, desire food (the objects of desire)

issues.span: just as poison is aroused by the perception of suspicion
issues.evidence: དུག་བསླང་བ is "takes/swallows poison" (bo-rangjung 5-17 reads དུག་བླངས་པ; bo-mipham 5-17: "thinking 'the poison has gone inside'"; Skt viṣasaṃjñata abhyupaiti). The poison is not "aroused"; a person, on suspecting, believes they have taken poison.
issues.fix: just as one who, through a suspicious perception, thinks they have taken poison

issues.span: Through the perception of that self, truly impermanent,
issues.evidence: The line says the perception of that self is unreal (ཡང་དག་མིན, Skt abhūto), not that the self is "truly impermanent": bo-mipham 5-17 བདག་ཅེས་བྱ་བའི་ཡུལ་དེར་འདུ་ཤེས་པ་ཡང་དག་པ་མིན་པའི་རྟོག་པ་འབྱུང་ཞིང་ ... སྐྱེ་ཞིང་འཆི; bo-khenrab 5-17 the same (བདེན་པར་འདུ་ཤེས་པ་ཡང་དག་པ་མིན་པའི་ཀུན་རྟོག). Skt also has sadā "always": they are always born and die. The English wrongly predicates impermanence of the self.
issues.fix: through the unreal perception of that self, are continually born and die

issues.span: without anything becoming an affliction or completely pure
issues.evidence: འདི་ལ་གང་ཡང་ཉོན་མོངས་རྣམ་དག་འགྱུར་མེད་པ means that in this (ultimate reality) no one/nothing becomes afflicted or purified (Skt na hy atra kaścid yo kliśyati śudhyate vā; bo-mipham 5-18 གང་ཟག་གང་ཡང་ཉོན་མོངས་པར་གྱུར་པ་དང་ ... རྣམ་པར་དག་པ་ཉིད་དུ་འགྱུར་བ་ཡང་མེད་པ). The English makes affliction itself the thing that something "becomes", obscuring that there is no one who is afflicted or purified.
issues.fix: in this, there is nothing that becomes afflicted or purified,

issues.span: If all of them were to generate
issues.evidence: The verse closes with the concessive ཡང (བསྔོ་ཡང་ "even though ... they dedicate"; bo-rangjung 5-19 བསྔོ་ཡང༌, bo-mipham 5-19 "ཡང་ཡོད་མོད་ཀྱི"), setting this vast merit against the next verse, where a single day of practising the perfection of wisdom surpasses it. The English drops the concession ("If ...") and leaves the sentence without a main clause.
issues.fix: even if all of them were to generate

issues.span: all fireflies, living creatures, and spirits
issues.evidence: སྲོག་ཆགས་འབྱུང་པོ་ཐམས་ཅད is a single phrase "all living beings/creatures" (Skt prāṇabhūtām), whose faint light is eclipsed; bo-mipham 5-25 and bo-khenrab 5-25 treat it as creatures with a little light, not as a separate class of spirits. What is overpowered is their light.
issues.fix: all fireflies and all living beings

issues.evidence: ཐབས་ཐོབ་གྱུར་ཏེ here means obtaining the means of ruling the kingdom (bo-mipham 5-27 རྒྱལ་ས་ལ་དབང་བའི་ཐབས་ཐོབ་པར་གྱུར་ཏེ; Skt paṭṭadhārī "wearing the royal diadem"), through consecration, in the prince parable; "skillful means" in the doctrinal sense does not fit.
issues.fix: when he obtains the means (of rule) and is established in the kingdom
